title: The 2009-2025 sigma0 26.5 oxygen low off southern California is a loss inside water types that agrees with an earlier offshore transition-zone and gyre loss, not with subarctic or tropical water
abstract: Question: what part of the CalCOFI oxygen low on the sigma0 26.5 surface is a change of water mix, and which source region carries the rest? Approach: on a fixed isopycnal, salinity fixes the water type. We split each CalCOFI cast anomaly (8,973 casts, 1984-2025) into a water-mix term from the 1984-1996 oxygen-salinity relation and a within-water-type term. We measured the same within-type change in GLODAPv2.2023 bottle data in seven regions, and tested a two-end-member mixing line that has no parameter fitted to CalCOFI. Main findings: from 1984-1996 to 2009-2025, CalCOFI oxygen fell by 21.9 umol/kg; the within-type term was -14.9 (95% interval -18.6 to -12.0) and the water-mix term -6.9. In 1997-2008 the water-mix term was larger (-9.2 against -4.6). The within-type loss had a remineralization signature (PO4* change -0.016) and was largest in the freshest, offshore water (r = 0.79 with longitude), not in the productive inshore band. Upstream, the within-type change in 1997-2008 was -20.1 in the transition zone and -17.3 in the eastern gyre, but -5.7 (interval includes zero) in the subarctic Line P region and +2.2 in Pacific Equatorial Water. The mixing line from the transition zone and gyre predicts a CalCOFI loss of -16.7 (-20.6 to -13.0) against -15.2 observed; from the subarctic source it predicts -3.0. A lag fit gives about 10 years (leave-one-cruise-out 9-11, bootstrap 0-12). Main limitations: few upstream cruises (one transition-zone cruise after 2008), GLODAP calibration limits for phosphate, two end members only, and no separation of slower ventilation from faster respiration in the upstream source.

citations.reason: We use its CalCOFI per-cast isopycnal tables, core stations, QC and climatology, and explain its post-2006 failure of the salinity proxy.
It showed that the 2007-2025 CalCOFI low is unprecedented since 1950 and is an AOU gain; we split that AOU gain into a water-mix and a within-type part.
It showed that Line P subarctic water did not carry the loss; we confirm this with GLODAP and identify the transition zone and eastern gyre as the source that agrees.
It showed that tracer-age ventilation shares are unreliable in the North Pacific; our source test needs no tracer age.
